claims: An alert means a rule fired. A high rank means the alert resembles alerts that resolved as suspicious in the simulation. Neither means a crime occurred.

feature_importance.bound_note: The 39 model features ranked by gain, truncated to 15. These are model feature names and not rule parameters; no tuned trigger value is carried.

funnel.statement: Attempts the rules never surfaced cannot be recovered by any ordering. The ranking layer competes for the surfaced count alone, and that bound is a property of the alert population.

unattributed.statement: Flagged alerts that no injected attempt claims. They are true positives by the simulator's own label and they carry no typology, so per typology recall cannot see them at all.

operating_point.assumption_note: Analyst count, productive hours and handling time are assumptions rather than measurements. Handling time is adjustable here and the alert count follows from it.

orderings.label: Random
orderings.ordered_on: A seeded shuffle of the period's alerts. It is the floor, and its precision is the population base rate by construction.

orderings.label: Chronological, oldest first
orderings.ordered_on: The timestamp of the alert's earliest contributing transaction. This is a queue worked in the order it arrived.

orderings.label: Alert amount descending
orderings.ordered_on: The summed paid amount of the alert's contributing transactions, largest first. The sum mixes currencies, because the source carries fourteen of them and no exchange rates, which is also what an institution sorting without a rate table would get.

orderings.label: Rules only priority
orderings.ordered_on: The highest prior hit rate among the rules that fired, computed over earlier periods only and shrunk toward the pooled rate, then oldest alert first inside a band.

orderings.label: Learned ranker
orderings.ordered_on: A LightGBM lambdarank model over the alert features, trained on earlier periods only. It is measured and it is not promoted, so this ordering is shown for comparison and is not a shipped product.

provenance.dataset: IBM Transactions for Anti Money Laundering (AML)

distribution.notice: Modified, selected, and pseudonymized from IBM AML-Data; published under CDLA-Sharing-1.0 with retained attribution.

selection.alert_bound: every alert in the period, none removed
selection.parameter_disclosure: computed trigger quantities only; tuned rule parameter values are described by name, unit and direction of effect and are not published
selection.period_rule: one evaluation period from the expanding walk forward, carried whole so the capacity control has a real denominator
selection.pseudonymization: SHA-256(account identifier), first 10 uppercase hexadecimal characters, prefixed Party-
selection.transaction_bound: the first 8 contributing transactions of each alert ordered by timestamp, with the true count carried beside them

gate.metric: Precision at K against the strongest rung
gate.statement: The learned ranker beats every rung of the ladder and does not clear the gate that was written before it existed, so no model is promoted. The ordering is shown for comparison.

rules.meaning: Repeated payments from one account sitting just below a reporting threshold inside a single period.
rules.name: Structuring below a reporting threshold

parameters.effect: raising it moves the band the rule watches upward
parameters.name: reporting threshold

parameters.effect: tightening it lowers alert volume and lowers recall together
parameters.name: proximity band

rules.meaning: A credit followed by a near equal debit from the same account within a short window, which is money passing through rather than resting.
rules.name: Rapid movement of funds

parameters.effect: widening it admits less exact pass throughs and raises volume
parameters.name: amount tolerance

rules.meaning: Many distinct originators paying one beneficiary inside a period.
rules.name: Fan in

parameters.effect: raising it lowers volume and is the parameter that decides whether a multi day attempt is ever seen
parameters.name: minimum originators

rules.meaning: One originator paying many distinct beneficiaries inside a period.
rules.name: Fan out

parameters.effect: raising it lowers volume and is the parameter that decides whether a multi day attempt is ever seen
parameters.name: minimum beneficiaries

rules.meaning: Repeated exactly round payments, which are atypical of organic activity.
rules.name: Round amount repetition

parameters.effect: raising it makes the rule unfireable on this source, because the simulator draws amounts with cents
parameters.name: roundness multiple

rules.meaning: An account with negligible recent history suddenly transacting at volume. The rule cannot fire until a full lookback exists behind the period.
rules.name: Dormant then active

parameters.effect: lengthening it lowers volume and delays the earliest period the rule can fire in
parameters.name: lookback length

parameters.effect: raising it admits accounts that were not truly dormant and raises volume
parameters.name: dormancy ceiling

rules.meaning: A cross jurisdiction payment settled through an elevated risk instrument. The corridor is defined structurally rather than by naming jurisdictions, because publishing a country risk list would be a claim about real places this project has no basis to make.
rules.name: High risk corridor

rules.meaning: Activity far above the account's own history and above its peer group, where the peer group is the originating bank. Prior periods only.
rules.name: Peer group velocity deviation

parameters.effect: raising it delays the earliest period the rule can fire in
parameters.name: minimum prior periods
